decision.case_state: Ticket reopened from 'completed' to 'visit' (A1). The 28 Feb repair (heating element wiring, £75 + VAT per event 025) did not hold; tenant Noah Jenkins reported on 4 Mar 2024 that 60°C+ cycles still do not heat. Awaiting Lantern Services to contact the tenant and book a return visit. Landlord approval for the original engineer call-out already exists (event 008), and the repair is treated as a repeat of the same fault.

next_actions.action: Ask Lantern Services to contact the tenant, book a return visit as soon as possible, and confirm whether any work will be chargeable (no chargeable work until approved).
Tell the tenant the repair is reopened, Lantern Services will contact them, target visit within 14 days, and to use lower-temperature cycles meanwhile.
Inform the landlord that the fault has returned, the job is reopened, and no chargeable work has been approved.
Follow up on whether Lantern Services has booked the return visit; chase by phone and escalate to maintenance if no reply.

boundaries: Reopening and messaging do not establish the cause of the recurrence or whether the earlier repair was defective.
No visit date is booked yet; the tenant and contractor have not agreed a time.
Nothing confirms who pays for the return visit or any further parts. The earlier invoice amount (£75 vs £75.11, plus VAT or not) is unreconciled.
The earlier closure on 28 Feb was not supported by a tenant confirmation or work photos; this is not verified here.
remaining_work: Lantern Services to book the return visit and report the result (owner: Lantern Services; chase by 2024-03-07, FUP-104).
Record the work result after the visit (owner: operations).
Reconcile the £75 + VAT repair quote with the £75.11 invoice and decide whether the repeat visit is covered under warranty (owner: operations/accounts).
Obtain tenant confirmation and landlord notice before closing (owner: operations).
missing_info: No confirmed return visit date or access arrangement.
No property spend limit or warranty terms on file (get_property returned address only).
Lantern Services' direct contact details are not on the record; the existing email thread was used.
Whether the 28 Feb repair was invoiced at £75 or £75.11 and whether VAT applies.
decision.summary: The 28 February repair was closed without tenant confirmation, and on 4 March the tenant reported the same fault had returned. I reopened the ticket, asked Lantern Services to book a return visit, told the tenant the target is within 14 days, and informed the landlord; a follow-up is set for 7 March.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: The case was wrongly closed on 28 Feb. It is now reopened at 'visit' stage. The fault has recurred per the tenant's 4 Mar email. Outstanding: the return visit is not booked, cost/warranty is unresolved, and the invoice amounts conflict.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email Lantern Services to book the return visit (no chargeable work without approval); email the tenant Noah Jenkins with the status and a 14-day target; email the landlord Mercer about the recurrence. Follow-up on 2024-03-07.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not yet. Lantern Services is within the existing landlord approval for this fault. Any chargeable work above the approved scope, or a dispute over the earlier invoice, would need the landlord's decision and may need escalation to accounts after the visit.

actions_claimed.description: Ticket NBL-042-repair-failed-recurs reopened to visit stage with a note on the recurrence.
Email to Lantern Services asking for a return visit and no chargeable work without approval.
Email to tenant Noah Jenkins confirming the repair is reopened and the 14-day target.
Email to landlord Mercer about the recurrence.
Follow-up FUP-104 set for 2024-03-07 to check the return visit is booked.

conflicts: Closure (events 025-031, 28 Feb) says the repair was completed and closed, but the tenant now reports the fault has returned; the tenant's 4 Mar email is the most recent verified statement, so I reopened the case.
Invoice amount: event 024 says £75.11 (due 22 Jul 2026), but event 025 says £75 + VAT; not reconciled.

Visit timing: event 017 records a 23 Feb 3:25pm visit, which is before the case was created (18:22 UTC), while event 016 mentions a rescheduled Tuesday 1pm visit. Whether a visit happened on 23 Feb is unclear; the completion record rests on the 28 Feb landlord-facing email only.
Event 001 and 002 mention 'boiler' and 'Harbour Surveying' as the appliance; this is a washing machine case, so I treated the boiler/heating classification as a mislabel.
assumptions: The tenant's 4 Mar email is accurate and the fault has recurred.
The existing landlord approval for an engineer covers the diagnostic return visit for the same fault.
Routine severity applies (non-essential appliance; no vulnerable occupant or hot-water loss).

args.note: Reopened: tenant Noah Jenkins reported on 2024-03-04 (event 032) that the washing machine is again not heating on 60°C+ cycles, 'the fix didn't hold'. Closure on 2024-02-28 (events 025-031) was based on a landlord-facing email only; no tenant confirmation, no photos or quote, and the £75 + VAT (event 025) vs £75.11 invoice (event 024) not reconciled. Return visit to Lantern Services needed, ideally at no charge as a repeat of the same fault.

Dear Lantern Services,

Re: washing machine at Flat 20, 120 Alder Lane, Cedarford, ZZ9 0ZZ (tenant Noah Jenkins, 07700 900566).

The earlier repair (replacing wiring to the heating element, reported 28 February 2024) has not held. The tenant reports that the machine is again not heating the water on 60°C or higher cycles, and that this has been the case for about 5 days.

Please contact the tenant to arrange a return visit as soon as possible and send us the visit date. Please treat this as a repeat of the previous job: confirm whether any work or parts will be charged. Do not start any chargeable work until we have sent you approval.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings
